name: Monaco
tagline: Two square kilometres of rock, casino and Grand Prix circuit, wedged between France and the sea.
summary: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world and the most densely populated, built vertically up a cliff because there is nowhere else to go. It is not in the EU or Schengen in its own right, though you enter through France and will not notice a border. For a visitor it is a half-day: the old town on the rock, the casino, the harbour, and the fact that a Formula One circuit runs through all three.

season.note: The Grand Prix takes the last weekend in May and doubles every price in the region. Spring and autumn are warm and manageable; August is hot and full.

getting_around: Walk, and use the public lifts — a network of them climbs the cliff for free. The train from Nice takes twenty minutes and is by far the best way in.
food: Barbagiuan, a fried chard and ricotta pastry, the actual national dish
Socca and Niçoise cooking, shared with the coast either side

festivals.where: The principality and the Alps behind

know: Not in the EU or Schengen as a member, but inside the Schengen travel area in practice via France.
The casino requires ID and refuses entry to Monégasque citizens by law.
Beach access is largely paid; the free public beach is at Larvotto.

regions.name: The Rock & the Harbour
regions.summary: The old town on its promontory, the port below, and Monte-Carlo along the bay.

cities.name: Monaco-Ville
cities.summary: The medieval quarter on the rock: palace, cathedral, and an oceanographic museum built into the cliff face.
highlights: The Oceanographic Museum, founded by a prince who was a serious scientist
The changing of the guard at 11:55, briskly
The Exotic Garden and the cave beneath it

experiences.name: Walk the Grand Prix circuit
experiences.summary: 3.3 km of ordinary public road: the tunnel, the hairpin, the harbour chicane. It takes forty minutes and recalibrates what you think those cars are doing.
